products.name: Acrobat and Acrobat Services
products.title: Adobe Acrobat for enterprise and the Adobe Acrobat Services APIs
products.what: Adobe's PDF products for business, as one box: the Acrobat apps for creating, editing, protecting and signing PDFs, licensed and deployed through the Admin Console, and Acrobat Services, cloud APIs that create, convert, generate, extract, tag, seal and embed PDFs inside your client's own applications.

source.title: Adobe Developer: Acrobat Services APIs introduction

products.notes: Two things share this box and should not be mixed up. Lines AB01 to AB03 and AB11 are the Acrobat apps, which Adobe sells as enterprise plans (Acrobat Studio, Premium, Pro and Standard) assigned to named users in the Admin Console; this is mostly IT work with a small partner share. Lines AB04 to AB10 and AB12 are Acrobat Services, the developer APIs, where most partner work sits. Adobe's developer pages still say Document Services in places, and Experience Manager pages say Document Services APIs or Document Cloud PDF Viewer, not Acrobat. The PDF Embed API is a free offering that needs only a client ID; the PDF Services API is measured in Document Transactions, and Document Generation, PDF Extract, Accessibility Auto-Tag and Electronic Seal come with it. The APIs process documents in the United States unless the Europe region is configured, and credentials stay on a server. A client that already has the AEM Forms Communications APIs (AF12 to AF15) generates documents there from XDP templates; AB05 is the Word-template route and the two should not both be sold for the same documents. Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none.
prereqs: Named user licenses for Acrobat, assigned through product profiles in the Admin Console
For AI Assistant: its license in the same Admin Console as the Acrobat license
For the APIs: credentials kept on a server, never sent to end user devices
For API volumes above the free allowance: paid credentials under a separate written agreement with Adobe
For the PDF Embed API: a client ID registered for the website domain it is used on
For document processing outside the United States: the Europe region, available once PDF Services API is purchased

prereq_sources.quote: Each license is assigned to a single user.
Both the Acrobat license and the AI Assistant license must appear in the same Admin Console to assign them to users.
SDK credentials should not be sent to untrusted environments or end user devices.
Paid credentials enable a greater processing quota and require entering into a separate written agreement.
If the client ID is incorrect or you are using it on a domain other than the one you registered, then the PDF preview is blocked with an error message.
Adobe PDF Services APIs use United States as a default region to process all the documents.

tiers.name: PDF Services API

tiers.quote: The latter two APIs and their SDKs are bundled into Adobe PDF Services API as part of a paid offering.

products.name: Acrobat Sign
products.title: Adobe Acrobat Sign Solutions
products.what: Adobe's e-signature service: send documents for signature, collect electronic and digital signatures, and track every agreement with an audit report. The Acrobat Sign Solutions plan adds groups, configurable templates, custom send workflows, bulk sending from a file, the API and connectors for other business systems.

source.title: Adobe Help: Set up your Acrobat Sign company account

products.notes: These lines assume an Acrobat Sign Solutions account. Adobe's help states availability feature by feature for three plans: Acrobat Standard and Acrobat Pro (e-signing inside Acrobat, with several features not supported or not configurable), Acrobat Sign Solutions, and Acrobat Sign for Government, a separate environment. Check each line against Adobe's availability note where your client is on the government environment. Premium identity checks such as knowledge-based authentication are purchased separately, and a provider on the Digital Identity Gateway needs its own contract (SG07). API access is reserved for enterprise and developer tier accounts (SG09). Adobe's help documents connectors to systems outside Adobe only; those that matter most are product lines with an ext (SG10 to SG12). The connections to Adobe products are documented on the other product's side (AEM Forms, Workfront Fusion, Acrobat) or in tutorials (Marketo Engage). The Microsoft Power Automate experience inside Acrobat Sign is not a service here (see left_out). Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none.
prereqs: An Acrobat Sign Solutions account; Acrobat Standard and Acrobat Pro leave custom send workflows unsupported and templates not configurable
The account entitled through the Adobe Admin Console, for single sign-on and automatic user creation
An enterprise or developer tier account for API access
Purchased transactions for premium identity checks such as knowledge-based authentication
For a sandbox: an enterprise account with a success manager, and a separate entitlement

prereq_sources.quote: Acrobat Standard and Acrobat Pro: Not Supported
The Acrobat Sign account must be entitled through the Adobe Admin Console.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe PDF Services modules (Workfront Fusion)

gain.title: Document steps inside work automation
gain.text: Your client's Workfront processes produce and handle documents by themselves: a brief becomes a PDF, proofs are combined into one file, and data is read out of an incoming PDF into Workfront fields.

flows.what: Files and data from Workfront objects, sent to PDF Services for an operation

source.title: Experience League: Adobe PDF Services modules (Workfront Fusion)

flows.what: Generated, converted or combined PDFs and extracted data, written back to Workfront

source.title: Experience League: Adobe PDF Services modules (Workfront Fusion)

connections.label: Workfront Fusion's Adobe PDF Services modules generate, convert, combine and read PDFs inside a scenario
connections.availability: Not stated by Adobe for the pair; Adobe documents the Adobe PDF Services modules in Workfront Fusion.

availability_source.quote: With the Adobe Workfront Fusion Adobe PDF Services, you can extract data from a PDF file, or generate a new PDF file from data you supply.

prereqs: Workfront Fusion, which is an additional purchase on Select and Prime packages that lack Workfront Automation and Integration
The Adobe PDF Services API added to a project in the Adobe Developer Console, with OAuth Server-to-Server credentials
PDF Services API volume that covers the scenarios' operations

prereq_sources.quote: If your organization has a Select or Prime Workfront package that does not include Workfront Automation and Integration, your organization must purchase Adobe Workfront Fusion.
To create an OAuth Server-to-Server connection, you must add the Adobe PDF Services API in your Adobe Developers Console.
Paid credentials enable a greater processing quota and require entering into a separate written agreement.

lines.name: PDF steps in Workfront Fusion scenarios
lines.scope: Create the PDF Services connection in Workfront Fusion and build the scenarios your client needs, such as generating a PDF from Workfront data, converting and combining documents on a task, or reading data out of a PDF into custom form fields.
lines.evidence: PDF Services also allow you to combine, compress, or read metadata for a PDF file, as well as control password protection on the file.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe PDF Services modules (Workfront Fusion)

client.how: Your Workfront automations use Adobe's PDF services to create, convert, combine and read PDF files as part of a process, and the results are saved back to the work they belong to.
client.gain: Your teams stop preparing routine documents by hand, and the documents attached to your projects arrive in the format the next step needs.

connections.how: The PDF Viewer Core Component embeds a PDF stored as an asset in AEM, or at another address, on an AEM Sites page. The component uses Adobe's Document Services APIs (the PDF Embed API viewer), and an administrator sets a context-aware configuration for it before authors can use it. Authors then choose the viewer type and which tools visitors see.

source.title: Experience League: PDF Viewer Component (AEM Core Components)

gain.title: PDFs read on the page
gain.text: Your client's brochures, manuals and reports open inside the page in Adobe's viewer instead of sending visitors to a download, with the controls your client chooses.

flows.what: The PDF Embed API viewer, loaded on the page with your client's client ID

source.title: Experience League: PDF Viewer Component (AEM Core Components)

flows.what: The PDF file and the viewer options the author set in the component

source.title: Experience League: PDF Viewer Component (AEM Core Components)

connections.label: PDF Viewer Core Component embeds PDFs on AEM Sites pages through the PDF Embed API
connections.availability: Not stated by Adobe; the component is part of the AEM Core Components.

availability_source.quote: The Core Component PDF Viewer component embeds a viewer to display PDF files stored as assets on the page.

prereqs: A PDF Embed API client ID registered for each site domain
A context-aware configuration for the component, set by an administrator

prereq_sources.quote: If the client ID is incorrect or you are using it on a domain other than the one you registered, then the PDF preview is blocked with an error message.
The PDF Viewer Component leverages Adobe's Document Services APIs and requires your administrator to configure a context aware configuration in order to use these services.

lines.name: PDF Viewer component on site pages
lines.scope: Create the PDF Embed API client ID for your client's site domains, set the component's context-aware configuration, add the PDF Viewer component to the page templates, and agree the viewer type and tools authors use.
lines.evidence: The PDF Viewer Component leverages Adobe's Document Services APIs and requires your administrator to configure a context aware configuration in order to use these services.

source.title: Experience League: PDF Viewer Component (AEM Core Components)

client.how: PDFs stored in your asset library open in Adobe's PDF viewer inside your web pages. Your authors choose how the viewer looks and whether visitors can download, print or annotate.
client.gain: Your visitors read documents without leaving the page, on any device.

connections.how: Acrobat opens a PDF in the Adobe Express editor from its Edit menu and offers Express templates and image editing inside Acrobat. Stylizing a PDF copies it into a new Adobe Express file, while an edited or generated image updates in Acrobat directly. Administrators turn the integration off for a user group in the product profile, and Acrobat Studio includes Adobe Express Premium.

source.title: Adobe Help: Adobe Express features in Acrobat

gain.title: Better looking documents without a designer
gain.text: Your client's staff give reports, proposals and flyers a finished look from inside Acrobat, with your client's brand kits and templates where the plan includes them.

flows.what: A copy of the PDF, opened as a new Adobe Express file for design

source.title: Adobe Help: Adobe Express features in Acrobat

flows.what: Edited and generated images placed in the PDF; restyled files downloaded and brought back

source.title: Adobe Help: Adobe Express features in Acrobat

connections.label: Adobe Express design tools open from Acrobat's Edit menu, switched per user group in the product profile
connections.availability: Adobe says the integration is accessible with Acrobat Studio, Acrobat Pro or Acrobat Standard subscriptions, for individuals, teams and enterprise customers.

availability_source.quote: Accessible with Adobe Acrobat Studio, Acrobat Pro, or Acrobat Standard subscriptions.

prereqs: Adobe Express services left on in the product profile of the groups that use the integration
Acrobat Studio, or an Adobe Express plan, for brand kits, premium fonts and assets
A step to bring restyled files back, because changes made in Express do not merge into the PDF

prereq_sources.quote: Admins can turn off the integration for a user group by turning off the Adobe Express services via the product profile.
Acrobat Studio includes full access to Adobe Express Premium, removing limitations on fonts, brand kits, and premium assets.
Changes made in Express will not automatically merge with Acrobat.

lines.name: Express design tools for Acrobat users
lines.scope: Decide with your client which groups keep the Express integration on in their product profile, make your client's brand kits and templates available to them, and show teams how stylizing a PDF, editing images and bringing a file back work.
lines.evidence: Admins can turn off the integration for a user group by turning off the Adobe Express services via the product profile.

source.title: Adobe Help: Adobe Express features in Acrobat

client.how: Your staff open a PDF in Adobe Express from inside Acrobat to restyle it, edit its images or start from a template, with your brand's colors, fonts and logos where your plan includes them.
client.gain: Your everyday documents look finished and on brand without a design request.

connections.how: The PDF Embed API sends viewer events, such as a document opened, pages viewed, downloads, prints and searches, to an Adobe Analytics report suite. The report suite ID is passed when the viewer is created, and two processing rules in Adobe Analytics map the events and their attributes to variables.

source.title: Adobe Developer: PDF Embed API analytics

gain.title: Know which documents are read
gain.text: Your client sees which PDFs on its site are opened, how far people read, and what they download or search for, in the same Adobe Analytics reports as the rest of the site.

flows.what: PDF viewer events and their attributes, such as the file name and page number

source.title: Adobe Developer: PDF Embed API analytics

connections.label: The PDF Embed API viewer sends PDF viewing events to an Adobe Analytics report suite
connections.availability: Adobe says an organization that already subscribes to Adobe Analytics gets PDF analytics by default, after a few setup steps.

availability_source.quote: If your organization already subscribes to Adobe Analytics, rich PDF analytics is yours by default.

prereqs: Adobe Analytics on the site, instrumented with the same report suite ID the viewer is given
Two processing rules in the report suite that map the viewer's events and attributes to Analytics variables

prereq_sources.quote: You must ensure that Adobe Analytics is instrumented using the same reportSuiteId for the website where you are embedding the PDF Viewer.
You'll need to create two rules and configure them so that you can map collected events and event attributes to Analytics variables.

lines.name: PDF viewing events in Adobe Analytics
lines.scope: Pass your client's report suite ID to the embedded viewer, create the processing rules that map PDF events and their attributes to Analytics variables, and build the report on documents opened, pages read, downloads and searches.
lines.evidence: To automatically receive PDF analytics events, pass the Analytics report suite ID when creating the AdobeDC.View instance.

source.title: Adobe Developer: PDF Embed API analytics

client.how: The PDF viewer on your pages reports to Adobe Analytics when a document is opened, read, downloaded, printed or searched, and those events appear in your reports beside your other site data.
client.gain: You see which documents your visitors read and how far they get, so you know which ones are worth keeping up to date.
